page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-48 is an x86_64 network-optimized virtual machine provisioned with 48 vCPUs across 24 dedicated physical cores on a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon 8581C processor. The hardware configuration features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and 372 GB of system memory, providing 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor includes hardware support for vector, matrix, and cryptographic instructions, including AVX-512, AMX (Tile and INT8), VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned without local storage devices and does not include hardware accelerators or bundled public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluation shows top-tier single-core compute performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2247.0 and high single-threaded decompression rates of 15.25 GB/sec in bzip3. Multithreaded performance is consistently strong, demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 19286.0, PassMark CPU score of 56797.87, and software compilation metrics reaching 47344.0. In artificial intelligence inference workloads, the AMX-equipped cores deliver top-tier throughput for small models, achieving 388.63 tokens/sec in text generation and 3496.55 tokens/sec in prompt processing on a 135M model, alongside 244.54 tokens/sec prompt processing on 7B models.

Memory throughput varies based on working set sizing, recording 3887.58 GB/sec in cached 16 KB read tests, while large uncached 256 MB blocks drop to 144.42 GB/sec read and 61.75 GB/sec write bandwidth. Database operations and key-value transactions register in the mid-tier bracket, processing 56.07 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring 21463.97 in PassMark database benchmarks. Static web serving throughput remains strong at 73.86 GB/sec.

The dense allocation of 372 GB memory relative to dedicated compute cores provides qualitative resource efficiency for memory-heavy operations without incurring the overhead of discrete GPU accelerators. Because the machine lacks local NVMe disks, operational performance depends entirely on remote network storage. This instance profile serves large-scale in-memory workloads, network-intensive middleware, enterprise application compilation, and CPU-based vector matrix inference pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-48 is a network-optimized virtual server powered by a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon 8581C x86_64 processor. The configuration allocates 48 dedicated vCPUs (24 physical cores), a 260 MB L3 cache, and 372 GB of system memory, delivering a 7.75 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. It incorporates Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions but includes no discrete GPUs, complimentary public IPv4 addresses, or local storage disks. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates top-tier single-core metrics in Geekbench and bzip3 decompression, strong multi-core processing in software compilation and PassMark testing, and fast text generation on small language models via matrix instructions. Memory bandwidth is high in cached operations but scales down during uncached block operations. This architecture fits memory-intensive applications, static web serving clusters, large-scale data processing pipelines, and CPU-driven integer and matrix inference workloads.
